facts.text: La Boca’s name, meaning “the mouth” in Spanish, references its position near the confluence of the Los Pinos and San Juan rivers.
The Los Pinos River borders La Boca to the east, flowing southward into Navajo Lake and joining the San Juan River.
La Boca sits in a high‑desert zone with a semi‑arid BSk climate, experiencing hot summers up to 95°F and cold winters dropping below 10°F.
Mule deer, pronghorn, coyotes, and golden eagles roam the scrubby shrub‑steppe surrounding La Boca, while endangered pikeminnow thrive in nearby river habitats.
Spanish explorers, including the 1776 Dominguez‑Escalante expedition, mapped routes through the San Juan Basin, linking Santa Fe to the Colorado River.
The 1962 completion of Navajo Dam on the San Juan River boosted water resources and spurred modern growth in La Boca.
